newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds were stable at the close on Monday ahead of Treasury auctions on Tuesday and Wednesday, dealers said.

"The market was really quiet today. Outside because of the U.S. elections and within domestic borders because of auctions," a dealer said. Tomorrow the Spanish Treasury will tender three and 10-year bonds, with five and 15-years offered Wednesday.
Comments by the Bank of Spain governor on EMU barely affected the market, dealers said. Luis Angel Rojo said EMU entry could be a problem for many countries if the EU economy fails to recover.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds widened a little to 178 basis points from 172 bps this morning, while the differential over Italian Btps fell to 32 bps from 35 bps.
"The Italian market will outperform Spain because inflation is lower in Italy," said Alessandro Ceccaroni, trader at UBS in London. The differential could fell to zero in the coming days, he said.
The market was also quiet ahead of tomorrow's U.S. presidential election, with results possibly influencing the dollar.
